attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, describing OpenAI's position in his own voice.

semantics.note: Accurately states his claim about what OpenAI argued. 'Would crush' is kept as his own description of the exemption, not as a separate claim to be scored.

contract.note: Reading 'exemption' in its everyday sense, as legal room to use protected work (including fair use), is fair and normal. Fair use is commonly called an exception to copyright. Not scoring the evaluative 'crush' part is also fair. The result depends on this reading of 'exemption'.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report (Jan 2024), before the post: OpenAI said building top models without copyrighted work would be 'impossible' and that it believes its training is lawful.
OpenAI's own Jan 2024 statement that training is fair use. It is primary evidence of what OpenAI argued. It rules out the idea of a newly requested statute, but fits the contract's reading.

reviews.rationale: Before the February 2024 post, OpenAI publicly said it would be impossible to train leading models without copyrighted material, and claimed fair use as legal permission. Under the fair ordinary reading of 'exemption', the necessity-plus-permission argument Marcus describes is confirmed. His view that this would crush creators is not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps his qualifier 'as far as I can tell'. That phrase signals the basis of his knowledge rather than a probability, so the claim is still a firm assertion. Labelling it causal (costs explain the absence of profit) is reasonable.

contract.note: Choosing calendar 2023 and company-wide net results is a fair ordinary reading. Running costs only have to contribute, not be the sole cause. The requirement to establish an accounting basis is strict but applies equally to support and contradiction.

evidence.note: Reports a 2022 loss from an unspecified, estimated measure. That is a different period from the 2023 target, and it does not separate out running costs.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no readable record of OpenAI's 2023 company-wide profit or loss, no accounting basis, and nothing that isolates the contribution of generative-AI running costs. The only item covers 2022 and is context only. The available evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the condition: $7T of infrastructure running at full capacity. Rendering 'metric shit ton' as 'enormous' is faithful.

contract.note: Requires the condition to actually be met (infrastructure built and running at full capacity) and reads the energy phrase in its ordinary sense. This is fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure about Stargate capacity commitments, published before the evaluation date. It shows neither $7T of completed infrastructure nor its energy use at full capacity.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional with no deadline. Nothing in the packet shows that about $7T of AI infrastructure was built and run at full capacity, so the condition is unknown and the forecast cannot be scored. The early-resolution rule has not been met.
